# Generate and accept a selection master

## Do a check of the work unit

Read the cycle record.
Do a check of the owner identifier (ID), skin IDs, mode, and request limits.
Process only the declared skin IDs.
Use one status record for each skin.

If a locked selection exists, do a check of its hash and review.
Reuse it when both values match.
Do not make a new request for that skin.
Stop when a recorded file has an unexpected hash.

## Measure the style source

Resolve the approved style reference from the controlling art contracts.
Examine it at equal displayed figure height.
Measure its visible bounds.
Record its face or display share.
Record its body split, lower-body share, and width relationships.

Copy these measurements into the current cycle record.
Do not put old character measurements in a reusable prompt.
Keep anatomy for the declared human or mechanical species.
Reject chibi construction and prestige-portrait construction.

Match these properties:

- Use restrained adult exaggeration.
- Use one readable role silhouette.
- Use one immediate visual joke.
- Use varied dark contour weights.
- Use expressive interior lines.
- Use large clean color shapes.
- Use broad hard-edged color values.
- Use neutral white balance.
- Keep warm color local.

## Resolve identity

Use the affected private study for a fictional or mechanical identity.
Use the two-stage method for an approved real-person-inspired identity.

For the two-stage method:

1. Examine the supplied identity image privately.
2. Crop to identity features only.
3. Remove text, logos, flags, and venue details.
4. Generate one private shoulder-up style-transfer design.
5. Give the approved style reference the style role.
6. Give the crop the identity role.
7. Use a fully illustrated result.
8. Reject photographic texture and lighting.
9. Save the accepted design in the cycle directory.

Do not upload the identity photograph to the final request.
A direct photograph can keep realistic skin.
This can cause a mixed face-and-body style.

## Construct the final request

For a two-stage identity, give Flare two illustrated references.
Give the approved style reference the full-body style role.
Give the accepted identity design the identity role.

For another identity type, use the applicable private study.
Use only references that the active contracts permit.
Do not upload another character as identity content.
Do not upload a rejected candidate.

Define the identity, construction, clothing or chassis, prop system, facing, and gesture.
Define all required exclusions.
Use the current cycle measurements.
Use the approved figure height and safe margins.
Use the background method in the cycle record.
Prohibit text, logos, extra subjects, and extra props.

Run a dry run before a paid request.
Do a check of the model, quality, size, background, reference order, and hashes.
Send one request after the dry run passes.
Write the request result to the cycle record.

## Review the candidate

Reject these defects:

- The proportions do not match the measured style source.
- The identity becomes generic.
- The face keeps photographic rendering.
- The face and body use different styles.
- Visible anatomy is malformed.
- A required prop is missing or duplicated.
- The image has a global warm wash.
- The image has forbidden matte color on the subject.

Examine the raw candidate before preparation.
Apply only the approved background preparation.
Examine the prepared result on light and dark backgrounds.
Examine the face or display at source size.
Examine all visible hands, appendages, props, and extremities.

Run alpha and color validation in an isolated directory.
Compare the candidate with the style source at equal figure height.

Record all seven candidate-review checks.
Bind the review to the prepared file hash.
Present the prepared candidate to the product owner.

## Lock the accepted selection

Get explicit product-owner acceptance.
Copy the prepared master to a unique locked path.
Record the raw, prepared, and locked hashes.
Record the acceptance decision and date.
Do not modify the locked file.

Use the locked selection as the sole pose reference.
Do not use the style source as a pose reference.
Do not use an identity image or private design as a pose reference.
Do not use a rejected selection or old pose as a pose reference.

In selection mode, stop after all declared selections are locked.
In package mode, continue with the pose procedure.
